title: Exceptional points in dissipative coupling polaron-polaritons
authors: A. J. Vega-Carmona, D. A. Mendoza, A. Camacho-Guardian, M. A. Bastarrachea-Magnani
abstract: Understanding how strong correlations and dissipation combine to shape collective quantum excitations is a central challenge in many-body physics. We investigate the effect of dissipative light-matter coupling on strongly interacting exciton-polaritons in the presence of a biexciton resonance, which gives rise to polaron-polariton quasiparticles. We show that the interplay between many-body correlations and non-Hermitian coupling generates anomalous dispersion relations and exceptional points in the polaron-polariton spectrum. The location and coexistence of exceptional points are controlled by the dissipative coupling and the relative decay rates of the excitonic and photonic constituents, allowing them to emerge across different polaron-polariton branches. These results identify dissipative polaron-polaritons as a versatile platform for exploring non-Hermitian many-body physics with tunable light-matter quasiparticles.
summary: This paper theoretically explores polaron-polaritons, quasiparticles formed by strongly correlated excitons coupled to photons. It demonstrates that incorporating dissipative light-matter coupling leads to the emergence of anomalous dispersion and exceptional points (EPs) in the system's spectrum. These EPs provide a tunable platform for studying non-Hermitian many-body physics.
main_problem: The study investigates how combining strong electronic correlations with dissipation affects collective quantum excitations, specifically focusing on polaron-polariton quasiparticles.
main_result: The interplay between many-body correlations and non-Hermitian coupling generates anomalous dispersion relations and exceptional points (EPs) in the polaron-polariton spectrum. These EPs are tunable by the dissipative coupling strength and relative decay rates.
method: The analysis employs finite-temperature Green's function formalism, solving for the polariton spectrum via the determinant of the inverse Green's function matrix after analytic continuation.
model_or_system: The system models exciton-polaritons in semiconductors exhibiting strong interactions mediated by a biexciton resonance. The Hamiltonian includes non-interacting terms, light-matter coupling (coherent and dissipative), and two-body interaction terms.
key_observables: Exceptional Points (EPs), anomalous dispersion relations, polaron-polariton branches ($E_{UP}/E_{LP}$), and level attraction.
important_parameters: Dissipative coupling ($\Omega_{Im}$), relative decay rates ($\gamma_x, \gamma_c$), biexciton energy ($\epsilon_B$), and system density.
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA) and relies on approximations like the ladder approximation for self-energy calculation in some parts.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate polaron branches vs. momentum/detuning, showing how increasing dissipative coupling causes curvature changes, negative mass effects, and the emergence of EPs; other figures map EP onset based on decay rates or BEC density.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem involving correlations and dissipation to deriving the full Hamiltonian and Green's function formalism. It then calculates the self-energy using pair propagators before analyzing the resulting spectrum, identifying EPs as key signatures of non-Hermitian physics.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant for AMO physicists working on open quantum systems and quantum optics because it uses engineered dissipation (non-Hermiticity) to control fundamental spectral features like exceptional points in interacting many-body platforms.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Dissipative coupling polariton branches. As a function of (a) momentum at zero detuning and (b) zero- momentum light-matter detuning. The upper branch (UB) and lower branch (UB) are indicated by black and red curves, respectively. Here, ΩIm/ΩRe = 0.9. Below, the condition for the emergence of EPs is shown as a function of dissipative coupling and (c) momentum and (d) detuning for several val- ues of ΩIm/ΩRe whose colors are indicated in the figure. The EPs are indicated with pink dots. We employ γc/2ΩRe = 0.1 and γx/2ΩRe = 0.9.

FIG. 2. Polaron-polaritons as a function of momentum (left) and detuning (right) for increasing values of the dissipative coupling: (a)-(b) ΩIm/ΩRe = 0.1, (c)-(d) ΩIm/ΩRe = 1.0, and (e)-(f) ΩIm/ΩRe = 1.5. In all cases we consider γc/2ΩRe = 0.1, γx/2ΩRe = 0.2, and a BEC density of 4πn↓/mx = 0.5. The dissipative coupling UB, MB, and LB are indicated by black, blue, and red solid lines, respectively. The dotted curves cor- respond to the results in (a) and (b). A black dashed line depicts the biexciton binding energy.

FIG. 3. Onset of EPs in polaron-polaritons as a function of detuning for zero momentum. The values taken for ∆γ are (a) −0.4, (b) −0.2, (c) 0, (d) 0.3, (e) 0.7, and (f) 0.9. We set ΩIm/ΩRe = 1.6. The color coding is the same as in Fig. 2. EPs are emphasized with green circles.
FIG. 4. Polaron polaritons as a function of detuning for a BEC density of 4πn↓/mx = 1.0. We employ γc/2ΩRe = 0.1, γx/2ΩRe = 1.7 and ΩIm/ΩRe = 0.1. The color coding is the same as in Fig. 2.
